bull.b: Sustained quarter‑over‑quarter growth in dispenses and $25.3M in Q2 product revenue demonstrate early commercial product–market fit. Durable adoption by prescribers, growing prescriptions and REMS certifications support a scalable U.S. launch that can transition the company toward recurring product revenues over the next 6–18 months.

A post‑offering cash balance near $1.7B materially extends runway to fund commercialization, regulatory filings and ongoing late‑stage trials. This reduces near‑term refinancing pressure, allowing management to execute launch plans and pivotal programs without immediate dependence on dilutive raises, improving execution optionality.

Statistically positive pivotal results and a planned sNDA materially de‑risk aficamten’s development trajectory, increasing the likelihood of label expansion and new indications. Combined with an existing MAPLE‑HCM PDUFA date, this strengthens the company’s product franchise and long‑term revenue potential independent of one‑time partner milestones.

bear.b: Very large negative operating and free cash flows reflect persistent high spending on launches and R&D. Even with current cash, sustained negative cash generation means the company will either need to realize meaningful product revenue growth or access capital markets again, creating structural financing and execution risk over the medium term.

Negative equity combined with substantial absolute debt levels indicates an impaired balance sheet that limits flexibility. This structural weakness raises refinancing and covenant risk, can increase cost of capital, and constrains strategic choices if product ramps or milestone receipts fall short of expectations.

Large year‑over‑year swings driven by licensing/milestone timing rather than recurring sales highlight unreliable top‑line predictability. Until MYQORZO and other assets produce sustained, predictable product revenue, planning and funding for continued commercialization and R&D will be more exposed to timing of partner events and one‑off payments.
